scenario.summary: Gamaredon (UAC-0010) uses the GammaLoad toolset, a multi-stage infection chain consisting of VBScript and PowerShell loaders. The malware fingerprints hosts, resolves C2 infrastructure via legitimate dead-drop services like Telegram and Telegraph, and maintains persistence using scheduled tasks that execute code stored in NTFS Alternate Data Streams.

meta.rationale: This hunt targets the Windows fleet, where GammaLoad registry and task mechanisms operate. Focus first on workstations with direct internet access, as they are the primary targets for initial access and DDR-based C2 discovery.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has established persistent access using GammaLoad VBScripts that manage C2 configuration via registry keys in HKCU\Console and execute via a high-frequency task invoking an Alternate Data Stream.

hunt.name: Gamaredon GammaLoad Multi-stage Persistence and Execution
hunt.description: GammaLoad is a modular VBScript loader used by Gamaredon (UAC-0010) for persistence and staging. It uses a failover mechanism for C2 discovery, storing active URLs in the Windows registry under HKCU\Console and using Dead Drop Resolvers (DDR) such as Telegraph and Telegram. This hunt identifies specific registry artifacts, correlates them with DNS requests to staging domains, and detects the 11-minute scheduled task used to launch a third-stage PowerShell loader from an Alternate Data Stream. By fanning out across registry, persistence, and network surfaces, the hunt provides a complete view of the GammaLoad infection chain that evades simple detection rules.
